quote: Yeah. We're just calling we saw we met with you a while back about solar.
stewart_read: For a recycled/repeat lead, the rep's re-intro is vague ('a while back') instead of anchoring specifics from the prior visit (what was discussed, what design or issue came up). This weakens legitimacy and wastes a chance to show the customer this is a real, tracked relationship, not a cold redial.
alternative_hypothesis: The rep may simply not have the prior-visit notes pulled up on this call, making vagueness a data-access issue rather than a rep skill issue.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to pull prior-touch notes before dialing recycled leads so the reconnect line can cite something specific (e.g., what was quoted, what stalled the deal).

quote: I was just gonna say the appointment would be pretty quick, not too long at all. We just come by. It'd be about thirty minutes just to show it to you.
stewart_read: Rep proactively anchors the time commitment before the customer even raises a time objection, which is the correct protocol move and likely defused a stall before it formed.
coaching_implication: This is a repeatable positive behavior — flag it as a model line for other setters handling busy/deferring customers.

quote: And then I think there were before, there was issues with credit. Is your credit score above 670 now?
stewart_read: Rep correctly remembers and re-raises the hard qualifier that previously blocked this lead, which is good diligence on a recycled lead.
coaching_implication: Good instinct to re-check the gate — the miss is what happens next, not the question itself.

quote: let me text you so you have my phone number. As far as scheduling, though, if the credit is good, can we do Monday morning or afternoon?
stewart_read: Rep proceeds to lock a day and time while the credit qualifier is still an open 'if.' The reactive read is that the rep prioritized keeping momentum toward a booked slot over resolving the gate first; the strategic read — that the rep intentionally booked provisionally and planned to confirm credit via the follow-up text — is partially supported by the later text-line reference to the 670 requirement, but the rep never gets a verbal commitment to check it before Monday.
alternative_hypothesis: Strategic: rep deliberately used the text-confirmation step as the mechanism to resolve credit before the visit, treating the phone booking as provisional by design.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to get a stated commitment on the call ('will you check your score before Monday and text me back?') rather than letting the qualifier ride silently into the confirmation text — this closes the loop instead of hoping it closes itself.

stewart_read: The rep never asks what originally interested this customer in solar or what has changed since the prior visit — a recycled lead is a prime spot to re-anchor motivation, and the call jumps straight from availability to qualifier without it.
coaching_implication: On recycled leads, the rep should ask a quick 're-anchor' question ('what got you looking into solar last time, has anything changed with your bill since then?') before scheduling — this call skipped that entirely.

quote: Yeah. Just credit score needs to be about 670.
stewart_read: The call ends without the standard button-up elements — no hour-block statement, no no-driving/computer language (irrelevant here since it's in-person, but no equivalent 'be home, we'll knock' framing), and no explicit 'is that fair?' handshake. The close is a soft 'you have a good one' rather than a locked confirmation.
coaching_implication: Coach the rep to close every booked call with an explicit recap and handshake line, even short reconnect calls — 'So Monday at 2, we'll swing by, that work?' locks the commitment more firmly than the current trailing goodbye.
